experiment: E1 sample efficiency vs scalar-reward RL

config.world: RuleWorld default (2 modules, 16 aspects, 2 conflicts, partial scoring, rich mu_f)

verdict: GEPA reaches 80%/90% of the oracle test score after mean 851/1685 rollouts (mean; reached in 100%/100% of seeds) vs scalar RL (rl_lr=2.0) 5326/8824 (mean over seeds that reached it; reached 100%/85%); median per-seed ratio RL/GEPA = 5.7x (80%) and 6.1x (90%). Claim '>=10x fewer rollouts': NOT reproduced at 10x at the 80% target, NOT reproduced at 10x at the 90% target. GEPA curve >= RL curve at 7/7 budgets <= 6000. Final test at equal-or-larger RL budget: GEPA 0.917 [0.910, 0.923] (B=6000) vs RL 0.902 [0.881, 0.922] (B=24000).
verdict_matched_ratio: At the paper's 1:4 budget ratio (GEPA B=6000 vs RL B=24000, paired over 20 seeds): GEPA - RL final test = +0.015 [-0.004, +0.035] (NOT significant); GEPA higher in 11, RL higher in 9 seeds; RL reaches the oracle test score in 7/20 seeds, GEPA in 0/20. GEPA reaches RL's final score in 11/20 seeds (5.0-35.6x fewer rollouts, median 11.5x). So 'outperforms RL' is judged at matched budgets by the curves above; at the 1:4 ratio it is a tie here.
